name: Leadbetter's theorem
scope_note: D(u_n) and D'(u_n) are hypotheses, as in the book.

name: Maxima of stationary sequences with an extremal index
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_measureReal_partialMax_le_pow.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1}
  {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] (hs : ProbabilityTheory.IsStationary X P)
  (hX : ∀ (t : ℕ), Measurable (X t)) {F H : CumulativeDistributionFunction}
  (hF : ∀ (x : ℝ), ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x = P.real {ω | X 0 ω ≤ x}) (hH : H.IsExtremeValueDistr)
  (As : ℕ → AffineIncrEquiv)
  (hlim :
    ∀ (x : ℝ),
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(As n • F).toStieltjesFunction x ^ n) Filter.atTop
        (nhds (↑H.toStieltjesFunction x)))
  {θ : ℝ} (hθ : ExtremeValueTheory.HasExtremalIndex X P θ) (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (x : ℝ) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun n => P.real {ω | ExtremeValueTheory.partialMax X n ω ≤ (As n)⁻¹ x})
    Filter.atTop (nhds (↑(H.pow hθ0).toStieltjesFunction x))
scope_note: theta > 0, as in the book; convergence of the iid maxima is assumed at every x.

name: H^theta is an extreme value law of the same type
scope_note: theta > 0.

name: Uniqueness of the extremal index
scope_note: Needs exceedance levels to exist, which is the strict notion of LLR.

name: The moving maximum has extremal index 1/2
scope_note: Any iid noise. HasExtremalIndex quantifies over level sequences, so it holds vacuously at any tau with no levels when the marginal has atoms; the strict form is in Dependence/StrictExtremalIndex.lean.

name: Basrak-Segers equivalence for a random vector
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.polar_iff.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E] {Z : Ω → ℝ}
  {V : Ω → E} {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hZ : Measurable Z) (hV : Measurable V) :
  (ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => P.real {ω | x < Z ω}) (-α) ∧
      ∃ μ,
        MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧
          ExtremeValueTheory.TendstoLawCond P (fun x => {ω | x < Z ω}) (fun x ω => (Z ω)⁻¹ • V ω)
            Filter.atTop μ) ↔
    ∃ ν,
      MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
        MeasureTheory.Measure.map Prod.fst ν = ProbabilityTheory.paretoMeasure 1 α ∧
          ExtremeValueTheory.TendstoLawCond P (fun x => {ω | x < Z ω})
            (fun x ω => (Z ω / x, x⁻¹ • V ω)) Filter.atTop ν
scope_note: Only (ii) <=> (iii) of the cited theorem, for one vector (Z, V). The statement for the whole series is hasTailProcess and related lemmas. The BS09 erratum was not consulted.

name: From the spectral tail process to the tail process
scope_note: One direction, as named. The tail process is realized on the product space Pareto x Q.

name: The time-change formula
scope_note: Measurable g >= 0 on finite windows. Stationarity is stated as shift-invariance of all finite windows.

name: The cluster ratio converges to the candidate extremal index
scope_note: Forward anticlustering at one level sequence is a hypothesis, as in the sources, and is necessary (Minimality.logEcho_blockRatio_ne). For |X|.

name: theta = candidate index under anticlustering
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.HasSpectralTailProcess.hasExtremalIndex_abs.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1}
  {Ω' : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩ' : MeasurableSpace Ω'} {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : ℤ → Ω → ℝ} {α : ℝ} {Q : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω'}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure Q] {Θ : ℤ → Ω' → ℝ} (hα : 0 < α)
  (hX : ∀ (t : ℤ), Measurable (X t)) (hΘm : ∀ (t : ℤ), Measurable (Θ t))
  (hstat : ExtremeValueTheory.HasShiftInvariantWindows P X)
  (h : ExtremeValueTheory.HasSpectralTailProcess P X α Q Θ) {r : ℕ → ℕ}
  (hr : Filter.Tendsto r Filter.atTop Filter.atTop)
  (hrn : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(r n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop (nhds 0))
  (hcond :
    ∀ τ > 0,
      ∀ (u : ℕ → ℝ),
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * P.real {ω | u n < |X 0 ω|}) Filter.atTop (nhds τ) →
          ExtremeValueTheory.ForwardAntiClusteringAt P X u r ∧
            ExtremeValueTheory.ConditionA (fun k => |X ↑k|) P u r) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.HasExtremalIndex (fun k => |X ↑k|) P
    (ExtremeValueTheory.candidateExtremalIndex Q Θ α).toReal
scope_note: Anticlustering and the block condition A(u_n) are hypotheses at every level sequence, as in the sources. A(u_n) carries the factorization of block maxima, so this is conditional on it; it is discharged only in the m-dependent entry. Stated for |X|.

name: theta = candidate index for m-dependent series
scope_note: Everything is derived from stationarity, the spectral tail process and m-dependence. Stated for |X|.

name: Strong mixing implies the block condition
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.conditionA_of_alphaMixing.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P]
  (hs : ProbabilityTheory.IsStationary X P) (hX : ∀ (t : ℕ), Measurable (X t)) {u : ℕ → ℝ}
  {r l : ℕ → ℕ} (hr : Filter.Tendsto r Filter.atTop Filter.atTop)
  (hrn : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(r n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop (nhds 0))
  (hlr : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(l n) / ↑(r n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0))
  (hα :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n / ↑(r n) * (ProbabilityTheory.alphaMixing X P (l n)).toReal)
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0))
  {C : ℝ} (hC : ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑n * P.real {ω | u n < X 0 ω} ≤ C) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.ConditionA X P u r
scope_note: A simple sufficient rate; nothing for beta-mixing beyond alpha <= beta.

name: Extremal index of a finite moving average
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.MovingAverage.hasExtremalIndex.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Z : ℤ → Ω → ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {α : ℝ}
  {m : ℕ} {ψ : ℕ → ℝ} (hZ : ∀ (i : ℤ), Measurable (Z i)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun Z P)
  (hident : ∀ (i : ℤ), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z i) (Z 0) P P)
  (hZ0 : ∀ (i : ℤ) (ω : Ω), 0 ≤ Z i ω) (hα : 0 < α)
  (hL : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => P.real {ω | x < Z 0 ω}) (-α))
  (hψ0 : ∀ (j : ℕ), 0 ≤ ψ j) (hψm : ∀ (j : ℕ), m < j → ψ j = 0)
  (hW : 0 < ExtremeValueTheory.MovingAverage.weightSum m ψ α) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.HasExtremalIndex (fun n => ExtremeValueTheory.MovingAverage.process m ψ Z ↑n) P
    ((Finset.range (m + 1)).sup' ⋯ ψ ^ α / ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), ψ j ^ α)
scope_note: Finite order, nonnegative coefficients and noise nonnegative at every point; the books allow signs.

name: theta = candidate index for infinite moving averages
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.InfiniteMovingAverage.hasSpectralTailProcess_and_hasExtremalIndex_of_summable_rpow.{u_1}
  {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Z : ℤ → Ω → ℝ} {ψ : ℕ → ℝ}
  {α δ : ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] (hZ : ∀ (i : ℤ), Measurable (Z i))
  (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun Z P)
  (hident : ∀ (i : ℤ), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z i) (Z 0) P P)
  (hZ0 : ∀ (i : ℤ) (ω : Ω), 0 ≤ Z i ω) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδα : δ < α) (hδ1 : δ < 1)
  (hL : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => P.real {ω | x < Z 0 ω}) (-α))
  (hψ0 : ∀ (j : ℕ), 0 ≤ ψ j) (hψ : Summable fun j => ψ j ^ δ) (hpos : ∃ j, 0 < ψ j) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.HasSpectralTailProcess P (ExtremeValueTheory.InfiniteMovingAverage.process ψ Z)
      α (ExtremeValueTheory.InfiniteMovingAverage.indexLaw ψ α)
      (ExtremeValueTheory.InfiniteMovingAverage.spectral ψ) ∧
    ExtremeValueTheory.HasExtremalIndex
      (fun n => ExtremeValueTheory.InfiniteMovingAverage.process ψ Z ↑n) P
      (ExtremeValueTheory.candidateExtremalIndex
          (ExtremeValueTheory.InfiniteMovingAverage.indexLaw ψ α)
          (ExtremeValueTheory.InfiniteMovingAverage.spectral ψ) α).toReal
scope_note: Nonnegative coefficients and noise; sum psi^delta < infinity for some delta < min(alpha, 1), which for alpha > 1 is stronger than the optimal condition.

name: Extremal index of the AR(1) process
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.AR1.hasExtremalIndex_of_pos.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Z : ℤ → Ω → ℝ} {φ α : ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P]
  (hZ : ∀ (i : ℤ), Measurable (Z i)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun Z P)
  (hident : ∀ (i : ℤ), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z i) (Z 0) P P)
  (hZ0 : ∀ (i : ℤ) (ω : Ω), 0 ≤ Z i ω) (hα : 0 < α)
  (hL : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => P.real {ω | x < Z 0 ω}) (-α)) (hφ0 : 0 < φ)
  (hφ1 : φ < 1) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.HasExtremalIndex (fun n => ExtremeValueTheory.AR1.process φ Z ↑n) P (1 - φ ^ α)
scope_note: 0 < phi < 1 and nonnegative noise: the negative coefficient and signed noise cases of Chernick are left out.

name: A stationary Markov chain with a prescribed kernel
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.RandomIteration.exists_isStationary_of_kernel.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [MeasurableSpace E] [StandardBorelSpace E] [Nonempty E] (K : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel E E)
  [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel K] (π : MeasureTheory.Measure E)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure π] (hπ : π.bind ⇑K = π) :
  ∃ g,
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      ExtremeValueTheory.RandomIteration.noiseKernel g MeasureTheory.volume = K ∧
        ProbabilityTheory.IsStationary
            (ExtremeValueTheory.RandomIteration.chain g Prod.fst fun n p => p.2 n)
            (ExtremeValueTheory.RandomIteration.canonicalMeasure π MeasureTheory.volume) ∧
          MeasureTheory.Measure.map Prod.fst
              (ExtremeValueTheory.RandomIteration.canonicalMeasure π MeasureTheory.volume) =
            π
scope_note: On a standard Borel space, indexed by N and forward only: no two-sided chain.

name: The forward tail chain for iid innovations
scope_note: The tail-chain condition is in random-function form |f(x,v) - a(v) x| <= b(v), regular variation of the marginal is a conditional-limit hypothesis, forward only. Not the general kernel condition of the sources.

name: theta = candidate index for ARMAX
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.ARMAX.hasExtremalIndex_candidate.{u_1} {φ α : ℝ} {Ω : Type u_1}
  {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P]
  {X₀ : Ω → ℝ} {V : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hφ0 : 0 < φ) (hφ1 : φ < 1) (hα : 0 < α) (hX₀ : Measurable X₀)
  (hV : ∀ (n : ℕ), Measurable (V n)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun X₀ (fun ω n => V n ω) P)
  (hiid : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun V P)
  (hlaw : ∀ (n : ℕ), MeasureTheory.Measure.map (V n) P = ProbabilityTheory.paretoMeasure 1 α)
  (hinv :
    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (Function.uncurry (ExtremeValueTheory.ARMAX.step φ))
        ((MeasureTheory.Measure.map X₀ P).prod (ProbabilityTheory.paretoMeasure 1 α)) =
      MeasureTheory.Measure.map X₀ P)
  (Q : MeasureTheory.Measure (ℕ → ℝ)) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure Q] :
  ExtremeValueTheory.HasExtremalIndex
    (ExtremeValueTheory.RandomIteration.chain (ExtremeValueTheory.ARMAX.step φ) X₀ V) P
    (ExtremeValueTheory.candidateExtremalIndex Q
        (ExtremeValueTheory.RandomIteration.spectralWalk fun x => φ) α).toReal
scope_note: Exact Pareto(1, alpha) innovations. theta and the candidate index are computed separately; the ARMAX spectral tail process is not stated, so this does not go through the theorem theta-equals-vartheta.

name: Uniqueness of the stationary law of X = AX + B
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.eq_stationaryLaw {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure (ℝ × ℝ)}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] (hA : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun p => Real.log |p.1|) ν)
  (hneg : ∫ (p : ℝ × ℝ), Real.log |p.1| ∂ν < 0)
  (hB : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun p => p.2.posLog) ν) (π' : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure π']
  (hinv :
    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (Function.uncurry ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.affine) (π'.prod ν) = π') :
  π' = ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.stationaryLaw ν
scope_note: Assumes log|A| integrable with negative mean, stronger than the book when P(A = 0) > 0 (Lean's log 0 = 0). Uniqueness part of the theorem.

name: Tail upper bound in the Kesten-Goldie regime
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.exists_stationaryLaw_tail_le {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure (ℝ × ℝ)}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] (hA : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun p => Real.log |p.1|) ν)
  (hneg : ∫ (p : ℝ × ℝ), Real.log |p.1| ∂ν < 0)
  (hB : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun p => p.2.posLog) ν) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 0 < κ)
  (h1 : ∫⁻ (p : ℝ × ℝ), ‖p.1‖ₑ ^ κ ∂ν = 1) (hnd : ¬∀ᵐ (p : ℝ × ℝ) ∂ν, |p.1| = 1)
  (hBκ : ∫⁻ (p : ℝ × ℝ), ‖p.2‖ₑ ^ κ ∂ν < ⊤) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hsκ : s < κ) :
  ∃ C,
    0 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (x : ℝ),
        0 < x →
          (ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.stationaryLaw ν) {y | x < |y|} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * x ^ (-s))
scope_note: Only P(|X| > x) = O(x^{-s}) for s < kappa. The Kesten-Goldie asymptotic c x^{-kappa}, the main result of the theory, is not proved, nor is the bound at s = kappa.

name: Existence of the GARCH(1,1) tail index
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.GARCH.exists_tail_index {α₁ β₁ : ℝ} {ζ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ζ] (hα₁ : 0 ≤ α₁) (hβ₁ : 0 ≤ β₁)
  (hlog :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun z => Real.log (ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.GARCH.coeff α₁ β₁ z)) ζ)
  (hneg : ∫ (z : ℝ), Real.log (ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.GARCH.coeff α₁ β₁ z) ∂ζ < 0)
  (hA0 : ∀ᵐ (z : ℝ) ∂ζ, ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.GARCH.coeff α₁ β₁ z ≠ 0) {S : ℝ} (hS : 0 < S)
  (hSi : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun z => ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.GARCH.coeff α₁ β₁ z ^ S) ζ)
  (hS1 : 1 < ∫ (z : ℝ), ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.GARCH.coeff α₁ β₁ z ^ S ∂ζ) :
  ∃ κ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 S,
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun z => ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.GARCH.coeff α₁ β₁ z ^ κ) ζ ∧
      ∫ (z : ℝ), ExtremeValueTheory.SRE.GARCH.coeff α₁ β₁ z ^ κ ∂ζ = 1
scope_note: Only the existence of kappa solving E A^kappa = 1. The tail of the GARCH process itself is not stated.
